# Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Definitions

- [statement] RTPP is not exposed for monitoring through the Atlas Administration API, although project settings can enable or disable it through that API. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md

## How it works

- [statement] Query-targeting ratios are diagnostic clues; MongoDB Search change-stream cursors can raise these ratios and trigger alerts. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Use RTPP to visually identify relevant database operations and evaluate query execution times; select a slow operation in the Slowest Operations table to open its Operation Details. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md · keywords: Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel · also: https://nljug.org/foojay/why-mirroring-production-in-dev-helps-you-avoid-costly-mistakes/
- [statement] RTPP may fail when db.currentOp() output exceeds its 4 MB per-sample maximum. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md
- [statement] Atlas documents one-second RTPP granularity. The Administration API can enable or disable RTPP, but cannot monitor its live panel data. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md
- [statement] RTPP targets ongoing operations; Atlas separately describes Query Profiler as providing historical slow-operation samples for up to seven days. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md · keywords: Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/analyze-slow-queries.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] COMPASS-10802 records an RTPP link returning 404 because /host/ was used instead of /metrics/. The issue was resolved with fix version 1.49.11. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-01) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/COMPASS-10802

## Facts and statements

- [statement] RTPP is Atlas's live triage panel for current database operations, network traffic, and host resources; it helps correlate query latency with resource pressure. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md · keywords: Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md
- [statement] RTPP is only available on M10+ clusters. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md · keywords: Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-use-mongodb-atlas-monitoring-for-cloud-deployments/view, https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74064516/finding-mongodb-cpu-usage-disk-utilization-ram-using-query-command
- [statement] RTPP's Slowest Operations uses db.currentOp(); Hottest Collections uses mongotop, and execution-latency charts use serverStatus opLatencies. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md
- [statement] Pausing RTPP freezes its display while underlying data collection continues; resuming restarts its line graphs with an empty display. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md
- [statement] The Kill Op control invokes db.killOp() on the selected running operation and requires an authorized project role. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md · keywords: Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md
- [statement] MongoDB documents one-second granularity for RTPP. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md
- [statement] RTPP uses mongostat for operation counters, mongotop for hot collections and db.currentOp() for the slowest current operations. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md
- [statement] The change-stream cursors that the MongoDB Search process (mongot) uses to keep MongoDB Search indexes updated can contribute to the RTPP query targeting ratio and trigger query targeting alerts if the ratio is high. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md
- [statement] Queryable Encryption hides affected collections from Hottest Collections and redacts query JSON involving encrypted fields. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md
- [statement] Vokint recommends pairing Atlas live operations and cluster signals with application OpenTelemetry traces; this is an integration recommendation, not proof that RTPP provides distributed tracing. (low confidence) — https://invokfung.github.io/blog/2025/08/19/mongo_26_opentelemetry_observability/
